evidence.note: Hope beat after failed get-up: 'Hitman reverses the leg drop — only 1 damage, and turns the tables!' while still GROUNDED — brief window before Hall resumes control.
Aggressive policy climbs into shared TOP_ROPE instead of Pull off the top rope 75% (Set up, shown in menu) — immediately punished by Superplex 29 (t18).
Groggy stretch (t22–t25) collapses choices to Reset/recover only (Shake / Desperation); Desperation strike deals the player's only offense of the match (4 damage).
Snowball finish: health [0,126], move_repetition_rate 0.5, single_choice_turns 8 (mostly get_up), near_fall_count 0 — no sustained trade-offs or comeback arc.
Groggy is clearly a modifier: 'Hitman is GROGGY — power moves and finishers are live!' while position stays STANDING/STANDING.
Pending-groggy on rise is explicit: 'Hitman rises — still groggy from the impact!' after get_up from GROUNDED.
Optimal counter is not hidden: Pull off the top rope 75% is curated alongside Climb — player simply picks the worse setup.
Grounded UX is readable but narrow: single choice 'Fight to your feet' with cover-vulnerability note; repeats at t7/t13/t15/t19/t21/t29/t31 (8 single_choice_turns).
Obvious rematch fork: take Pull off the top rope 75% instead of Climb while Hall is TOP_ROPE to deny the Superplex that drops Bret to 51 HP.
Second fork: Pull off 67% is shown again while Hall is TOP_ROPE; player hits the ropes and eats diving crossbody 20 (t28).
Desperation strike clears groggy and chips 4 — only glimpse of Bret offense; curiosity to see whether surviving groggy into standing Sharpshooter/path exists.

stickiness.rematch_reason: Concrete 'yank him off the top' forks at t17/t27 and a dramatic KO finish make retry cheap, but 8 get-up-only turns and zero player big spots keep rematch intent lukewarm.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 216 selecting Pull off the top rope (75%) on turn 17 instead of Climb, and again on turn 27 (67%) instead of Hit the ropes, to test whether denying Hall's top-rope payoffs opens a Bret offense window.

evidence.note: Superplex payoff: 'Hall snaps off superplex — Hitman takes 29 damage' with both GROUNDED — densest state shift of the bout.
Groggy stingers land twice (t22, t24) with clear live-finisher telegraph; t25 desperation clears haze with narrative 'fights through — the groggy haze lifts!'.

KO finish narrative: 'Hall snaps off razor's edge — Hitman takes 20 damage. Hitman crumples and doesn't move — they are out cold! *** KNOCKOUT — the match is waved off; Hall wins ***' — impactful, but no finish_sequence.delays_sec pin pacing and near_fall_count 0.
Player-side juiciness is thin: only 4 damage landed all match; log_uniqueness_ratio 0.7368 helped by CPU variety, not Bret spots.

top_issues.summary: Match is mostly grounded recovery: 8 single_choice_turns and move_repetition_rate 0.5 from repeated Fight to your feet; aggressive policy rarely sees a multi-intent menu with real offense.
Pure snowball to KO: Bret ends at 0 HP vs Hall at 126 after landing only a 4-damage desperation strike; reversals at t6/t16 never convert into sustained offense.

Aggressive player twice ignores curated Pull off the top rope (75% t17, 67% t27) and climbs/runs into Hall top-rope payoffs — intent labeling may undersell that Pull-off is the defensive/optimal answer.
top_issues.suggested_area: curation intent label for pull_off_top when opponent is TOP_ROPE

top_issues.summary: near_fall_count 0 and knockout finish skips pin-count delays; cover-available telegraph at t30 never becomes a near-fall beat.
top_issues.suggested_area: CPU finish choice pin vs KO / near-fall thresholds
